title: Settlement Basis: the Balance Due on a Vacation Package
content:
The balance due on a package among the Vacation Package Products is worked out from the package record and the lines standing on its ledger. Each quantity below is defined once, and the last of them is the figure collected.

**The package discount applied.** The package discount applied to the quoted price is nil.

**The discounted price.** The discounted price is the quoted package price reduced once by the package discount applied. The discount acts on the quoted price alone and never on the ledger lines.

**The promotional deposit shortfall.** The promotional deposit shortfall carried into the balance is nil.

**The agency service fee carried in.** The agency service fee carried into the balance is nil.

**The outstanding amount.** The outstanding amount is the discounted price, plus the signed total of the component lines standing on the ledger, plus the promotional deposit shortfall, plus the agency service fee carried into the balance, less the deposit already taken and less the instalments already taken. The component lines are totalled with their signs, so a component carrying a negative amount reduces the total rather than adding to it.

**The figure taken now.** The figure taken now is the whole outstanding amount.

**The currency presentation loading.** The currency presentation loading applied to the figure taken now is the whole of it and nothing more.

**The balance due.** The balance due is the figure taken now multiplied by the currency presentation loading, rounded to two decimal places and never less than nil. The rounding happens once, at the end.

## Worked through on hypothetical inputs

Take a package on the Escorted Tour Package whose record shows a quoted price of 4,000.00 USD. Its ledger carries component lines totalling 250.00 USD with their signs, one deposit line of 600.00 USD, and no instalment yet taken.

The package discount applied is nil, so the discounted price is 4,000.00 USD. The promotional deposit shortfall is nil and the agency service fee carried in is nil. The outstanding amount is 4,000.00 USD plus 250.00 USD, less 600.00 USD already taken as a deposit and nothing taken as instalments, giving 3,650.00 USD. The figure taken now is that whole amount. The currency presentation loading is the whole of it, so the figure stands at 3,650.00 USD; it is above nil, and rounded to two decimal places the balance due is 3,650.00 USD.

Were the same ledger to carry a component line of minus 100.00 USD as well, the signed total of the component lines would be 150.00 USD and the balance due would be 3,550.00 USD.
